newsitem.title: USA: In Home Health evaluating reimbursement decisions.
newsitem.headline: In Home Health evaluating reimbursement decisions.

text.p: In Home Health Inc said Thursday it is evaluating the impact of three decisions concerning disputed Medicare payments, some of which grant the company payment for claims while others deny payments.
The decisions are likely to affect whether the company is entitled to Medicare reimbursement for similar costs in subsequent years, it said.
The company said it is evaluating the impact of the three decisions on these subsequent years and on the company's other Medicare reimbursement disputes.
Based on its preliminary evaluation of the reasoning behind each decision, the company has identified $13 million in revenue which may not be realized, said Kari Schell, vice president-treasurer.

One case involved whether the company would be reimbursed for costs associated with its home care coordinator/community liaison personnel at certain company offices in fiscal years ending September 30, 1989 through 1992.

A U.S. District Court for Minnesota held that the company was not entitled to Medicare reimbursement for about $1.6 million of these costs incurred prior to June 1992, but was entitled to partial reimbursement of the costs for the period from June through September 1992.
The total costs for June through September 1992 were $300,000.

In another case the Department of Health and Human Services let stand a decision in the company's favor by the Department's Provider Reimbursement Review Board concerning the allocation of certain company branch office administrative costs in fiscal years 1990 through 1993. The amount of the reimbursement in dispute in this case was about $500,000.

In a third case, the Provider Reimbursement Review Board ruled that the company would be partially reimbursed for costs associated with its home care coordinator/community liaison personnel at certain company offices in fiscal years ending September 30, 1991 through 1993. The amount of Medicare reimbursement in dispute in this case was about $3 million.
As a result of this information, In Home Health said it has restated its per share earnings for the third quarter of fiscal 1997 to a loss of $0.89 from a reported loss of $0.14.

The loss was primarily due to the $13 million revenue adjustment, a $2 million restructuring charge previously reported and a preferred stock dividend. This was offset by an income tax benefit of $1.7 million.
The company said it has not yet decided whether to appeal the District Court decision.
In Home Health provides comprehensive health care services to clients in their own homes.
Shares of In Home Health fell 3/16 to 1-7/16 after a trading halt.
